title: Administration Secretary
description:
Trust: Hampshire & Isle of Wight Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust

Job Title: Administration Secretary

Department: Admin

Duration: This is a temporary role, and it is currently due to last roughly 2 months

Location: Antelope House, Brintons Terrace, Southampton, SO14 0 YG

Working Pattern: 37.5 hours per week, Mon - Fri, 9am - 5pm

Pay Banding: Band 3 £14.05 per hour

Job Reference: 92083

The postholder must have the following experience:

RiO (NHS System) experience

Job Description

To provide a comprehensive administration service to the clinical team and/or service.

The post holder will be responsible for the organisation of their own workload and delegated decisions/actions, as deemed appropriate by the Business Administration Manager.

KEY ACTIVITIES / RESPONSIBILITIES

To type correspondence using both copy typing and audio, including letters, minutes, and reports as indicated by the line manager.

Be responsible for administration support to nominated individuals.

To set up office systems and procedures to ensure that all documents can be retrieved easily.

Support the clinical team as required in diary management, meeting management, report writing, administering personnel files, communication of on-call rota, communication of roster changes and taking messages.

Organising meetings and taking minutes as necessary, typing and distributing to those appropriate.

Ensure that all typing and administrative duties are completed promptly and efficiently for the clinical team. This will include undertaking own secretarial duties as required.

To ensure effective communication with service users, relatives and carers, visitors, staff and others.

To ensure that all communication is within the boundaries of service user confidentiality and to seek guidance when unsure.

To provide support for onboarding new clinicians. This relates to processing new starter forms, acquiring necessary access and authorisations and required preparations for arrival.

To support the clinical team in relation to IT equipment provision. This relates to ordering, retrieval on ending of contracts, ensuring an accurate record is kept.

Co-ordinates establish and maintain a comprehensive paper and electronic filing system across the clinical team to include:
- Electronic filing
- Diary management
- Computerised databases, with relevant levels of access/restrictions.
- Data confidentiality

To document information in accordance with record keeping standards

To ensure that any information related to service user or other personal safety is communicated immediately to senior team members.

To ensure a comprehensive telephone service is provided to indicated staff, ensuring that messages are taken and given in a consistent and efficient manner.

To use the highest level of interpersonal skills when dealing with sensitive or contentious information.

To be responsible for the recording of all contacts with service users in the patient record whether primary (electronic) or secondary in line with the Trust s record keeping policy.

Create, develop and maintain professional supportive relationships with all members of staff.

To assist in the collection of data for the purpose of audit, research and service performance.

To be able to enter and retrieve information from spreadsheet databases.

To deal with incoming and outgoing mail as required.

Assist with subject to access requests as directed.

You ll learn the following whilst working at the trust:

1. An in depth understanding of the roles and responsibilities involved in working within the NHS

2. Knowledge of the systems used, to effectively complete your role to the highest standard at all times

3. A sense of teamwork, gained through working alongside and supporting colleagues from all levels, within the organisation

As a member of NHS Professionals, you have fantastic benefits:

Competitive pay rates - work this week, get paid next week

Essential support when you need it- 24/7 365 days - call us anytime

Multi locational - work across neighbouring Trusts

Manage your shifts and timesheets on the go - access your My Bank shift portal anywhere, anytime online or through your smartphone

Varied working options to suit your lifestyle - access to the Bank gives you options of ad hoc shifts or longer-term placements

Training and development opportunities - Keep up with the essentials and more

Build holiday allowance for every shift you work - your work life balance is important to us

Stakeholder pension scheme available - a flexible future for you and yours

Who are NHS Professionals?

We specialise in putting people in place to care. Every year we help thousands of dedicated candidates and highly skilled NHS workers enjoy better career opportunities, access to more shifts and a healthier work-life balance, giving more choice and control to our members.

As an equal opportunities organisation, NHSP is committed to the equal treatment of all current and prospective Bank members and does not condone discrimination on the basis of age, disability, sex, sexual orientation, pregnancy and maternity, race or ethnicity, religion or belief, gender reassignment, or marriage and civil partnership. We believe there is a strong case for the Equality, Diversity and inclusion agenda and we strongly encourage suitably qualified applicants form a range of backgrounds to apply.

Apply Today

By joining us you can look forward to a choice of flexible Bank shifts across any of our client Trusts in England, as well as the ability to develop professionally and gain experience in several wards or areas.

This role may require you to show evidence of vocational level 3 qualification or at least 2 years relevant experience.

Disclaimer

Please note, you will be contacted by email throughout the recruitment process, so please check your emails, including your junk/spam regularly. We regret we cannot contact everyone who is not selected for an interview, therefore if you do not hear from us within 21 days after submitting your application, please assume you have not been successful on this occasion.

title: Administrator - Construction
description:
Administrator - Construction / MOD Projects

Location: Southampton / Eastleigh, Hampshire
Salary: Competitive, dependent on experience
Employment: Permanent, Full-Time
Sector: Construction - Defence, Education & Commercial

The Opportunity

3 D Personnel are recruiting on behalf of a leading national construction contractor with an established presence across Hampshire and the South Coast.

Our client delivers a diverse portfolio of construction projects across the Ministry of Defence (MOD), Department for Education (DfE) and commercial sectors, ranging from new-build developments to complex refurbishment and infrastructure projects.

Due to continued growth and an expanding portfolio of MOD projects, they are seeking an experienced Administrator to join their established team based in the Southampton / Eastleigh area.

This is an excellent opportunity for an organised, proactive and experienced Administrator to join a reputable construction business, supporting project teams delivering high-profile defence projects across the region.

Key Responsibilities
- Provide comprehensive administrative support to project managers, site teams and senior management.
- Coordinate project correspondence, reports, meeting minutes and general documentation.
- Maintain accurate project records, databases, spreadsheets and filing systems.
- Assist with the preparation and distribution of project reports, presentations and contractual documentation.
- Coordinate meetings, appointments, diaries and internal communications.
- Support project teams with procurement administration, purchase orders and supplier correspondence.
- Assist with site administration, onboarding records, compliance documentation and project-related paperwork.
- Liaise professionally with subcontractors, suppliers, clients and internal departments.
- Ensure all administrative processes comply with company procedures and project-specific security requirements.

Experience & Requirements
- Previous experience in an Administrator, Project Administrator or Site Administrator position.
- Experience within the construction, engineering, infrastructure or defence sectors would be advantageous.
- Excellent organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.
- Strong IT skills, particularly Microsoft Office, including Word, Excel, Outlook and Teams.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
- High attention to detail and the ability to handle confidential information professionally.
- A proactive and adaptable approach, with the ability to work independently and as part of a wider project team.
- Previous experience supporting MOD or other public-sector projects would be beneficial but is not essential.

Security Clearance Requirements

Due to the sensitive nature of the MOD projects, applicants must be eligible to successfully complete Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) checks and obtain Security Check (SC) clearance.

Applicants must be able to provide suitable evidence of identity, nationality, right to work in the UK and relevant employment history. British citizenship and a valid British passport would be advantageous, subject to the specific project's security requirements.

What's on Offer?
- Permanent employment with a leading national construction contractor.
- Opportunity to work on high-profile MOD and defence-sector projects.
- An established and supportive regional team.
- Long-term career development and progression opportunities.
- Competitive salary and company benefits package.
- Exposure to a varied portfolio of construction projects across the South Coast.

How to Apply

If you are an experienced Administrator looking to develop your career within a leading construction business, we would welcome your application.

Please submit your CV to 3 D Personnel for a confidential discussion regarding this opportunity.

title: Document Controller - Construction
description:
Document Controller - Construction / MOD Projects

Location: Southampton / Eastleigh, Hampshire
Salary: Competitive, dependent on experience
Employment: Permanent, Full-Time
Sector: Construction - Defence, Education & Commercial

The Opportunity

3 D Personnel are recruiting on behalf of a leading national construction contractor operating throughout Hampshire and the wider South Coast.

Our client has a strong regional presence and an established portfolio of construction projects across the Ministry of Defence (MOD), Department for Education (DfE) and commercial sectors.

As part of their continued growth and ongoing delivery of high-profile MOD projects, they are looking to appoint an experienced Document Controller to join their Southampton / Eastleigh team.

The successful candidate will play an important role in maintaining accurate, secure and efficiently managed project documentation throughout the construction lifecycle, working closely with project managers, design teams, engineers and subcontractors.

This position offers an excellent opportunity to join a respected national contractor delivering technically challenging projects within a highly regulated environment.

Key Responsibilities
- Manage, maintain and control all project documentation in accordance with company procedures and client requirements.
- Administer electronic document management systems (EDMS), ensuring accurate filing, tracking, revision control and distribution of information.
- Coordinate the receipt, review, approval and issue of drawings, specifications, technical submissions and project correspondence.
- Maintain document registers, drawing schedules and associated trackers throughout the project lifecycle.
- Ensure project teams, consultants and subcontractors have access to the latest approved documentation.
- Monitor document submissions and approvals, highlighting outstanding information and potential delays.
- Support project managers, design managers and site teams with document control processes and reporting.
- Assist with the collation of quality assurance records, handover documentation and operation and maintenance manuals.
- Maintain strict confidentiality and appropriate access controls for sensitive MOD project information.
- Ensure all documentation is managed in accordance with contractual obligations, quality standards and project-specific security protocols.

Experience & Requirements
- Previous experience working as a Document Controller within the construction, engineering or infrastructure sectors.
- Experience working for a main contractor or on major construction projects would be highly advantageous.
- Strong understanding of construction documentation, drawing management and revision control procedures.
- Experience using electronic document management systems such as Asite, Aconex, Viewpoint, Autodesk Construction Cloud or similar.
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Office, particularly Excel, Word and Outlook.
- Excellent organisational skills, accuracy and attention to detail.
- Ability to manage large volumes of documentation across multiple projects and stakeholders.
- Strong communication skills and the confidence to liaise with project teams, subcontractors and external consultants.
- Previous experience on MOD, defence, government or other security-sensitive construction projects would be advantageous.

Security Clearance Requirements

Due to the nature of the MOD projects, applicants must be eligible to successfully complete Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) checks and obtain Security Check (SC) clearance.

Applicants must be able to provide suitable evidence of identity, nationality, right to work in the UK and relevant employment history. British citizenship and a valid British passport would be advantageous, subject to the specific project's security requirements.

Existing BPSS screening or SC clearance would be beneficial, although applicants who are eligible to undergo the required vetting process will also be considered.

What's on Offer?
- Permanent position with a leading UK construction contractor.
- Opportunity to work on prestigious MOD and defence-sector construction projects.
- Long-term career stability within an established regional business.
- Competitive salary and benefits package.
- Professional development and career progression opportunities.
- A collaborative working environment supporting projects across Hampshire and the South Coast.

How to Apply

If you are an experienced Document Controller seeking a long-term opportunity with a reputable construction contractor, we would welcome your application.

Please submit your CV to 3 D Personnel for a confidential discussion regarding the role.

title: Laboratory Administrator / Archivist (Data Co-ordinator)
company: DEKRA Organisational & Process Safety - Agency - Contract
description:
Laboratory Administrator / Archivist (Data Co-ordinator)

Location: Site Based, Southampton, SO16 7 NS
Contract: Up to 12 months FTC maternity cover
Salary: £12.71 per hour

Do you want to boost the future towards a safe, secure and sustainable world

At DEKRA we deal with future topics in every field of work: from vehicle inspection to cyber security, from product testing to clean energies or from automated driving to artificial intelligence.

We anticipate technical developments early on and drive industry transformation as thought leaders.

For the exciting tasks that lie ahead we are looking for skilled and passionate people who want to grow and achieve their best in a global team.

Enthusiasts wanting to do meaningful work and to make a contribution as a trusted partner for our clients and for society. People like you.

A Day in the Life and the Impact You'll Make

As a Data Co-ordinator, you'll play an important role in supporting our Laboratories team, helping to keep projects organised, samples accurately recorded and technical reports delivered on time.

From booking in samples and preparing study files to maintaining laboratory records and managing archives, you'll work across a varied role where accuracy, organisation and attention to detail really matter.

What You'll Do
- Manage the archive room, ensuring records are stored correctly and maintained in line with Good Laboratory Practice (GLP).
- Coordinate the booking-in and unboxing of samples, maintaining accurate sample records and databases.
- Prepare GLP and non-GLP technical reports for our Industrial Explosive Hazards, Regulatory Testing and Electrostatic laboratories.
- Maintain the Laboratories Master Schedule and Globex system.
- Liaise with clients regarding sample and test programme queries.
- Support project administration, including sales orders, consumables and financial information.
- Coordinate the return or destruction of study data and reports at the end of the archiving period.
- Support reception duties when required.
- Work collaboratively across DEKRA to identify opportunities to improve processes, efficiency and customer service.
- Work with laboratory teams to ensure test results and reports are delivered promptly.
- Maintain high standards of health, safety, data protection and information security.

What You'll Bring
- Strong attention to detail and a high level of accuracy.
- Good IT skills and confidence using technology and databases.
- Excellent organisation skills and the ability to manage competing priorities.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
- GCSEs in Science and English, or equivalent.
- Good knowledge of Microsoft Office.
- A positive, proactive approach and willingness to support colleagues.
- A strong team ethic and commitment to delivering excellent customer service.

What Success Looks Like
- Well-maintained laboratory records and archives.
- Accurate and timely sample booking-in and unboxing.
- High-quality technical reports delivered within agreed timescales.
- KPIs achieved across sample receipt, booking-in, reporting and archiving.
- Clear, professional communication with internal and external customers.

Why DEKRA

At DEKRA, our people make the difference. We value Responsibility for Safety, Entrepreneurship, Customer Orientation, Integrity and Team Spirit.

We encourage our people to be proactive, share ideas, solve problems and continuously look for better ways of working. Development within DEKRA will depend on business needs, as well as your ability, ambition and drive.

Let's create a safer world today. Apply now and join a team that values your expertise and passion.

At DEKRA we value your unique experiences, perspectives, and backgrounds. We are committed to an inclusive workplace for all team members.

title: Operations Support Coordinator
description:
- Operations Support Coordinator
- Southampton, Hampshire
- 6-month contract
- £32,000 to £35,000 per year (Pro-Rata)

Summary:

Our client is looking for an experienced, organised Operations Support Coordinator to support its UK operations team based in Southampton, working within roadside technology and traffic safety.

You will coordinate operational administration and customer reporting, while ensuring invoices, purchase orders and supporting records are accurate and processed on time.

Working closely with the Operations Manager, field engineers and contractors, you will help keep maintenance activities and customer projects running smoothly.

This position would suit someone comfortable managing competing deadlines, investigating discrepancies and following actions through to completion within a technical service environment.

- Maintain meeting actions, controlled documents and audit evidence, following up with relevant colleagues and contractors.

- Experience supporting technicians or maintenance teams within a technical, regulated environment.
- Practical experience processing invoices and purchase orders using an ERP system; SAP Business ByDesign experience is desirable.
- Advanced Microsoft Office skills, particularly Excel, with confidence maintaining spreadsheets and checking data accuracy.
- Experience gathering and analysing operational information to produce clear customer and senior management reports.
